question.text: If \(\mathrm{a}_0\) is denoted as the Bohr radius of hydrogen atom, then what is the de-Broglie wavelength \((\lambda)\) of the electron present in the second orbit of hydrogen atom? [n : any integer]

solution.text:
$r_n=\frac{a_0 n^2}{z}$
Also, $2 \pi \mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{n}}=\mathrm{n} \lambda$
Where $\lambda$ is de-Broglie wavelength
$\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{a}_0 \mathrm{n}^2}{\mathrm{z}}=\mathrm{n} \lambda$

For second orbit of H -atom
$\lambda=\frac{8 \pi \mathrm{a}_0}{\mathrm{n}}$
